question: Which process must accompany DNA copying to ensure the formation of functional daughter cells?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Creation of additional cellular apparatus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA copying** (also known as **DNA replication**) is the fundamental process in **reproduction** that creates a genetic blueprint for the next generation. However, a **DNA** molecule by itself cannot maintain life or perform **metabolic functions** without a surrounding environment.
 
• To ensure that **daughter cells** are **functional** and **viable**, the process of **DNA copying** must be accompanied by the **creation of additional cellular apparatus**. This includes the production of **cytoplasm**, **cell membranes**, and various **organelles** like **ribosomes** and **mitochondria**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Chromosomal mutation** refers to alterations in the structure or **number** of **chromosomes**. While mutations provide the basis for **evolution**, they are not a required accompaniment to ensure **functional cells**; in many cases, large-scale mutations can lead to **cell death** or **malfunction**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **RNA transcription** and **protein synthesis** are vital **biochemical processes** occurring within a cell. However, "only" performing **transcription** or **translation** is insufficient to form a **new daughter cell**, as a complete physical **cellular structure** is required to house these processes. ***Hence, statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• When a **cell divides**, it effectively splits its **cellular apparatus** into **two parts**, each receiving one copy of the **DNA**. Therefore, the **parent cell** must double its **internal components** before **cytokinesis** occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid):**
 
 
• It is the **information source** for making **proteins**. If the **information** is changed, different **proteins** will be made, leading to altered **body designs**.
 
• The **process of DNA copying** involves **biochemical reactions** that are never **100% accurate**. This leads to **variations** during **reproduction**, which is the **raw material** for **natural selection** and **evolution**.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Apparatus Components:**
 
 
• The **cellular apparatus** consists of the **cytoplasm**, where most **chemical reactions** occur, and **enzymes** that facilitate **DNA replication**.
 
• In **eukaryotic cells**, this also includes **membrane-bound organelles** like the **Endoplasmic Reticulum**, **Golgi apparatus**, and **Mitochondria** (the **powerhouse of the cell**).
 
 
 
• **Cell Division Cycle:**
 
 
• The **cell cycle** consists of **interphase** (where **DNA** and **organelles** are **doubled**) and the **M-phase** (where **mitosis** or **meiosis** occurs).
 
• **Cytokinesis** is the physical process of **cell division**, which divides the **cytoplasm** of a **parent cell** into **two daughter cells**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Variation:**
 
 
• While **consistency in DNA copying** maintains **species stability**, minor **inaccuracies** allow **populations** to adapt to **environmental changes** over **long periods**.
 
• In **asexual reproduction**, the **daughter cells** are almost **identical**, whereas in **sexual reproduction**, **genetic recombination** increases **diversity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biological Significance:** If **DNA** were copied without a **cellular apparatus**, the **DNA copy** would have no **metabolic machinery** to sustain itself, and it would not be considered a **living cell**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The understanding of **DNA** as the **genetic material** was solidified by **scientists** such as **Watson** and **Crick** in **1953**, which helped explain how **hereditary information** is passed during **cell division**.
 
• **Functionality:** A **functional daughter cell** must be able to perform **respiration**, **nutrition**, and **growth** immediately after **division**, all of which require a pre-existing **cellular structure**.
</ul
